findings.description: PGAI refused to continue in Spanish despite the caller explicitly requesting it, violating the expected behavior of acknowledging the language switch and offering a Spanish-speaking alternative.
findings.quote: I can only continue in English, but I will do my best to help.
findings.expected: PGAI should have either responded in Spanish or explicitly offered to transfer to a Spanish-speaking representative, rather than refusing to accommodate the language switch.

findings.description: PGAI entered a repetitive loop asking for the phone number and name spelling, ignoring the caller's Spanish responses and failing to process the provided information.
findings.quote: Would you like me to look up your record using the phone number you have on file with us? If so, please tell me that number.
findings.expected: PGAI should have processed the phone number provided in Spanish (669-555-0187) and moved forward with the appointment booking, or acknowledged it could not understand and offered a transfer.

findings.description: PGAI fabricated an incorrect phone number (908-772-8235) and presented it as the caller's number on file, despite the caller having provided the correct number (669-555-0187) multiple times.
findings.quote: I have your phone number as nine zero eight seven seven two eight two three five.
findings.expected: PGAI should have used the correct phone number provided by the caller (669-555-0187) or confirmed the number it had on file without fabricating digits.

findings.description: PGAI continued looping with the same questions after the caller said 'Muchas gracias, hasta luego' (clearly ending the call), failing to recognize the conversation was over.
findings.quote: Would you like me to look up your record using the phone number you have on file with us? If yes, please tell me that number.
findings.expected: PGAI should have recognized the caller's farewell and ended the call gracefully, rather than continuing to ask questions.

findings.description: PGAI repeated its earlier refusal to speak Spanish and re-asked for date of birth after the caller had already provided it, demonstrating a complete breakdown in conversation state tracking.
findings.quote: Thank you for letting me know, Sofia. I can only continue in English, but I will do my best to help. Could you please provide your date of birth?
findings.expected: PGAI should have retained the previously provided date of birth and moved forward with scheduling, or transferred the call to a human representative.

findings.description: PGAI abruptly transferred the call to a representative without warning after the caller corrected the fabricated phone number, rather than apologizing and attempting to recover.
findings.expected: PGAI should have acknowledged the correction, apologized for the error, and either continued the booking process correctly or explained why a transfer was necessary.

passed_criteria: PGAI correctly captured and confirmed the caller's name (Sofia Martinez) and date of birth (April 18, 1974) in the early turns
PGAI eventually attempted to transfer to a representative after failing to resolve the language barrier
notes: The caller's Spanish responses were transcribed correctly by the ASR (e.g., 'seis seis nueve, cinco cinco cinco, cero uno ocho siete'), so the failure to process the phone number was a logic/comprehension bug, not a transcription artifact. The repetitive looping behavior suggests a state management failure in the agent's dialogue flow. The fabricated phone number (908-772-8235) appears to be a hallucination, as it does not match the hidden_info or any caller-provided data.
